novel_features.name: Commitments extractor
novel_features.description: Surface every promise you made — "I'll send", "let me follow up", "by EOW" — across every recording, grouped by who you said it to, with the date and recording link.
novel_features.rationale: Plaud has speaker-diarized transcripts of every conversation but exposes no cross-recording aggregation. Only possible because we mirror transcripts to a local SQLite store with FTS5.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When the user asks "what did I promise people this week?", reach for this before opening any individual recording. The answer is a list, not a transcript.

novel_features.name: Recurring-topic trajectory
novel_features.description: Trace how often a topic comes up across your recordings over time. Bucketed by week or day. Shows emerging vs decaying signal with the speakers anchoring each bucket.
novel_features.rationale: Requires FTS5 over transcripts joined to recordings.start_time with bucketed aggregation. No single Plaud API call returns this shape.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When the user is wondering whether a concern is growing or fading, this command answers it in one query instead of opening 20 summaries.

novel_features.name: About a person
novel_features.description: Every utterance by one named speaker, across every recording, with ±1 segments of surrounding context. Optional topic filter for laser-focus.
novel_features.rationale: FTS5 over speaker-diarized transcripts is the join Plaud's app cannot serve. Requires the speaker dimension materialized in local SQLite.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pre-call prep: pull everything a person said about a topic in one read. Beats scrubbing recordings at 2x speed.

novel_features.name: Forgotten commitments
novel_features.description: Commitments you made that have no follow-up signal in any later recording. The set difference between things-you-said-you-would-do and things-you-actually-talked-about-again.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the commitment row set from #1 plus a left-anti-join over later transcripts. Pure local computation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surface the broken promises before the other person does. There is no other tool that knows what you said you'd do AND whether you followed through.

novel_features.name: Themes diff
novel_features.description: Top n-gram shingles in recent recordings vs the prior equivalent window. Frequency-based — no LLM. Output shows what's new this period, what's vanished, what's steady.
novel_features.rationale: SQLite tokenize + stop-word list + window comparison. Mechanical extraction, not generative summarization.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Monthly reviews without reading anything. The deltas tell you where your attention is shifting.

novel_features.name: Cross-meeting consistency
novel_features.description: Every utterance by one person about one topic, ordered chronologically across meetings, with prior + next segment as context. Read it to see whether their (or your) position has drifted.
novel_features.rationale: Requires FTS5 + speaker filter + start_time ordering. Per-recording view in Plaud's app cannot answer it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When you need to know whether a stakeholder has been saying the same thing over time. Drift detection without rereading every meeting.

novel_features.name: Silence detector
novel_features.description: People who used to appear in your recordings but haven't in N days. Last recording link + last topic mentioned. Surfaces relationships going cold.
novel_features.rationale: MAX(start_time) GROUP BY speaker — aggregate that requires the speaker dimension. Plaud's app has no speaker-as-entity view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: For managers and operators: which reports, customers, or stakeholders have gone quiet? The recording you need is the absence of one.

novel_features.name: Mentioned me
novel_features.description: Every time someone OTHER than you said your name in a recording. Pulls from the cached /user/me name and FTS5-filtered out your own segments.
novel_features.rationale: Cached user identity + FTS5 + speaker exclusion. Requires both the user store row and the speaker dimension.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Third-party mentions of the user — who's talking about them and what they're saying. No other Plaud tool surfaces this.

narrative.headline: Every conversation, queryable — your transcripts as a searchable history, not a feed.
narrative.value_prop: Plaud captures every meeting with speaker diarization. plaud-pp-cli mirrors that history to a local SQLite store with FTS5, then asks the questions the app cannot: what did I promise across all my recordings, who said what about a topic over time, which commitments did I drop, who has gone quiet. A raw `sql` escape hatch lives at the bottom for anything we didn't anticipate.
narrative.auth_narrative: Auth uses Plaud's own user-app endpoint (POST /auth/access-token, email + password) — same as the community libraries. Tokens last ~300 days; the CLI silently re-logs in 30 days before expiry. For a no-password path, `auth login --chrome` lifts the JWT directly from your logged-in browser. Region (us / eu / ap) auto-detects on the first call.

quickstart.comment: Verify token, region, and reachability before syncing anything
Walk every recording into the local SQLite store: list, transcripts (speaker-diarized), summaries, file tags
Every promise you made in the last month with no follow-up signal — the headline command
Speaker-scoped FTS — pull everything one person said about one topic across every meeting

quickstart.command: plaud-pp-cli sql 'SELECT speaker, COUNT(*) FROM transcripts GROUP BY speaker ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10'
quickstart.comment: Raw SELECT-only SQL escape hatch when the typed commands fall short

troubleshoots.symptom: Login returns status -302 with a `domains.api` payload
troubleshoots.fix: Region mismatch — the CLI auto-retries at the correct host. If it loops, set `--region eu` (or `us`/`ap`) explicitly on `auth login`.

troubleshoots.symptom: 401 on every command after working previously
troubleshoots.fix: JWT expired or was rotated server-side. Run `plaud-pp-cli auth login` again. If that fails, try `auth login --chrome` after logging into web.plaud.ai.

troubleshoots.symptom: `recordings transcript <id>` returns empty for old recordings
troubleshoots.fix: Recordings created before March 2026 use the S3 fallback path. Re-run `sync` so the CLI fetches the unauthenticated S3 transcript URL from `/file/detail`.
Run `sync` first — FTS5 indexes are built locally from transcripts, not the API. `doctor` confirms whether the store has rows.
Speaker labels may be `Speaker 1` / `Speaker 2` from raw ASR; rename them in app.plaud.ai then re-`sync`. The CLI follows whatever speaker names Plaud has assigned.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for plaud-pp-cli when the user wants to query their conversation history as data: "what did I promise across all meetings", "who said X about Y over time", "have I been consistent". Don't reach for it for one-recording-at-a-time consumption — Plaud's app or the official CLI are fine for that. The transcendence commands (commitments, topic, about, forgotten, themes, cross-meeting, silence, mentioned-me) only work after `sync` has populated the local SQLite mirror.

recipes.title: Sunday-night planning
recipes.explanation: Sync first, then pull every open commitment from the last week. `--select` narrows the response to what the agent needs — plaud transcripts can be huge.

recipes.title: Pre-call prep for a renewal
recipes.explanation: Every utterance by Sandra mentioning pricing across the last quarter of meetings. Faster than scrubbing recordings.

recipes.title: Monthly thematic review
recipes.explanation: What's growing and what's fading in your recent conversations. Frequency-based, no LLM call — runs entirely on local data.

recipes.title: Who has gone quiet
recipes.explanation: Speakers who appeared in past recordings but not in the last 21 days. For managers and operators tracking relationships.

recipes.title: Cross-meeting drift check
recipes.explanation: Every utterance from Marcus mentioning launch date, ordered chronologically. Read the rows top to bottom — that's the drift.

recipes.title: Raw SQL when typed commands fall short
recipes.command: plaud-pp-cli sql 'SELECT speaker, COUNT(*) AS n FROM transcripts GROUP BY speaker ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10' --json
recipes.explanation: SELECT-only escape hatch. FTS5 MATCH is supported. The store schema is documented in the README.

what did Sandra say about renewal
what topics are coming up in my meetings
